title: Like Empty Beer Cans and Butts
text:
Like empty beer cans and cigarette

butts gone out, so have my days been.

Like figures passing across a television screen

and disappearing, so has my life passed.

Like automobiles that sped along the highways

with girls' laughter and radio music...

And beauty passed quickly, like the model of cars

and the songs on radios that went out of fashion.

And nothing has remained of those days, nothing,

except empty cans and extinguished butts,

laughter in faded photos, torn tickets,

and the sawdust with which at dawn they swept the bars.
editorial_note: The source has a typo in 'television'; the translation follows the intended image of a life passing across a screen.

editorial_note: This variant repeats the beer-can elegy under a shorter catalog title.

title: Psalm 4
text:
Hear me because I call upon you, God of my innocence

You will free me from the concentration camp


How long, leaders, will you be senseless?

How long before you stop speaking with slogans

and saying pure propaganda?


There are many who say:

who will free us from their atomic weapons?


Lord, make your serene face shine

over the Bombs


You gave my heart a joy

greater than the wine they drink at their parties


As soon as I lie down I am asleep

and I have no nightmares or insomnia

and I do not see the specters of my victims

I do not need Nembutals

because You, Lord, give me security
editorial_note: The translation preserves the psalm's biblical address recast against camps, propaganda, and atomic fear.

title: Here He Passed on Foot...
text:
Here he passed on foot

through these streets,

without employment or post


And without a peso


Only poets, whores

But


remember him when

you have concrete bridges,


Great turbines,

tractors, silver granaries,


good governments.


The National Guard

is looking

for a man


a man hopes

tonight to reach

the border


the name

of that man

is not known


there are many

more men

buried in

a ditch


The number and

the name of those

men are not known.


Nor is the place known

or the number of ditches.


The National Guard

is looking for a man


A man hopes

tonight to leave

Nicaragua
editorial_note: The source appears fragmentary after 'Only poets, whores'; the translation preserves that break and the shift to the fugitive.

title: Deliver Me, Lord...
text:
Deliver me, Lord

from the S.S. from the N.K.V.D. from the FBI from the G.N.


Deliver me from their War Councils

From the rage of their judges and their guards


You are the one who judges the great powers

You are the judge who judges the Ministers of Justice

and the Supreme Courts of Justice


Defend me, Lord, from the false trial!

Defend the exiles and the deported

the accused of espionage and sabotage

condemned to forced labor


The weapons of the Lord are more terrible

than nuclear weapons!

Those who purge others will also be purged


But I will sing to you because you are just

I will sing to you in my psalms / in my poems
editorial_note: The translation keeps the litany of security forces and courts under divine judgment.
